“What do you need me for?” I asked.

Tavin pointed to the map.

“The roadwright owns the repair. The Guild lead owns the contract. The haulers own their carts. The gate clerk controls the queue,” she said.

“And?” I asked.

“And all four can do their jobs correctly and still make a mess,” Tavin said.

I smiled. She noticed.

“That's what the report says you are good at.”
patches.after:
“What do you need me for?” I asked.

Tavin put one finger on the repair lane.

“Roadwright repairs. Guild lead owns the contract. Haulers own their carts. Gate clerk owns the queue.”

Her finger stayed on the gap between them.

“You watch what none of them can see from where they're standing.”

I smiled.

“That's what the report says you are good at.”
patches.reason: At boundary-hunt heat, Tavin should own the explanation through the map and compress the abstract And exchange into her operational way of assigning responsibility.

“It is a blister.”

“It is two blisters.”

I looked. There were, in fact, two.

“That's rude.”

“Your skin?”

“Yes.”

She held out her hand. I gave her mine. She examined the palm without fuss.

“No casting today.”
patches.after:
“It is a blister.”

Hessa took my hand before I finished defending it and turned the palm toward the light.

“Two.”

I looked. There were, in fact, two.

“That's rude.”

“No casting today.”
patches.reason: Mara's Hessa is stronger when procedure interrupts Greg's verbal defense instead of participating in every joke beat.

“You paid for this?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“I wanted a bath.”

He stared. I stared back.

“Are you sick?”

“No.”

“Did Hessa tell you?”

“No.”

“Antonius?”

“No.”

“Woman?”

“No.”

His eyebrows went up.

“Man?”

“No.”

“Then why?”

“I wanted a bath.”

He sat on the edge.

“That's worse.”
patches.after:
“You paid for this?”

“Yes.”

“Who made you?”

“Nobody.”

Jorren stopped with one foot in the water.

“Hessa?”

“No.”

“Antonius?”

“No.”

“Romance?”

“No.”

He lowered himself into the pool, still watching me.

“You just wanted a bath.”

“Yes.”

“That's worse.”
patches.reason: The over-hot take lets Jorren seize the exchange, compress repeated yes/no beats, and make Greg's voluntary leisure the actual joke rather than the list itself.

patches.before:
Arlo shifted the bundle under his arm.

“Greg.”

“What?”

“You said you're busy.”

“I am.”

“So be busy.”

He turned again. This was intolerable.

“Can the customer do later?”

Arlo stopped.

“After midday.”

“How far?”

“East lamp works.”

I knew it. Not far.

“Could we go after?”

“Yes.”

“Why didn't you say that?”

“Because you said you're busy.”
patches.after:
Arlo shifted the bundle under his arm.

“Greg. Go spar.”

“Customer later?”

“After midday.”

“East lamp works?”

“Yes.”

“Then I'll meet you after.”

Arlo had already started walking.

“That was always an option.”
patches.reason: Boundary-hunt authority allows the whole exchange to collapse around Arlo's process-minded impatience. The information and Greg's choice survive with much less conversational circling.

“Not a number,” I said.

“Good.”
patches.after:
“How many?”

Hessa did not answer.

“Two?”

Still nothing.

I sighed.

“If you give me a number, I'll turn it into permission.”

“Good,” Hessa said.

I disliked everyone competent.
patches.reason: At higher rehearsal authority Hessa can force Greg to articulate the rule himself. Silence becomes instruction and removes explanatory dialogue she does not need to speak.

“What does that mean?”

“You've stopped arriving as if every hour of your life is an emergency.”

“That sounds insulting.”

“It is complimentary.”

“Badly.”

“I have talents.”

He tapped the folder against the table.

“Next week, if you want, I can give you two fixed storehouse periods instead of arranging them piecemeal,” Antonius said.
patches.after:
“What does that mean?”

Antonius opened the folder.

“It means I can schedule you now without wondering whether you'll vanish into whatever caught fire in your head that morning.”

“Complimentary?”

“Very.”

He slid three possible storehouse periods across the table.

“Pick two.”
patches.reason: Desmond gets more authority to turn Antonius's observation directly into a transaction. The joke remains, but the folder and offered choices do the scene work.

patches.before:
Pessa looked at my board.

“You write too much.”

“I've been told.”

“Write less.”

“Which parts?”

“Things that change decisions.”

“That is subjective.”

“Yes.”

I hated experts. Dorn said, “Farmer red face doesn't change decision.”

“I didn't write red face.”

“You thought it.”

“Yes.”

Pessa took my board.
patches.after:
Pessa took my board and crossed out half the first entry before speaking.

“Too much.”

“Which parts?”

She handed it back.

“If removing it doesn't change the next decision, remove it.”

Dorn pointed at the farmer complaint.

“Red face survives?”

“I didn't write red face.”

“You thought it.”

I hated experts.
patches.reason: Pessa should edit before explaining. At boundary-hunt heat her physical correction leads and her principle follows, while Dorn keeps the social joke alive.
